newsitem.title: INDIA: India's L&T breaks ground for IT park.
newsitem.headline: India's L&T breaks ground for IT park.

text.p: Indian engineering giant Larsen and Toubro Ltd (L&T) has begun work on a 15-billion-rupee information technology park in the southern city of Hyderabad, officials said on Tuesday.
Industry Minister Murasoli Maran laid the foundation stone for the project, whose first phase, a 400,000-square-foot complex, is scheduled to be completed by September 1998.

The Hyderabad Information Technology and Engineering Consultancy City, or HITEC City as it is called, is a joint venture between L&T and the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corp (APIIC), a state-run agency.
L&T holds 89 percent of the equity and APIIC the rest.

HITEC City will have sophisticated communication facilities, including a 64 kbpc/2 Mb satellite earth station, uninterrupted power and water supply, central air conditioning, video conferencing and multimedia facilities, officials said.
The total project outlay estimated for HITEC City is 15 billion rupees, L&T said in a statement. It will be completed in six phases over a 10-year period.
